source_text:
τῷ δευτέρῳ τελοῦντας τὴν ἑορτὴν, σφάζοντάς τε τὸ ἱερεῖον, εἰς τύπον Χριστοῦ, κατὰ τὸν τοῦ Πάσχα νόμον, οὐχ ἑτέρους εἶναι νομιοῦμεν, ἢ ὅτι τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἐπὶ τῇ κατὰ Χριστοῦ μιαιφονίᾳ μεμολυσμένους, καὶ γραφὴν ἔχοντας εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν, τὸ ἐμπαροινῆσαι εἰς τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ. Οἱ γάρ τοι τοιοίδε τῆς ἁγίας ἡμῶν ἑορτῆς ἀπώλισθον ἀναγκαίως. Ὑστερίζουσι δὲ καὶ διημαρτήκασι τοῦ καιροῦ καθ' ὃν ὁ τῆς ἁπάντων ζωῆς ἀρχηγὸς τετελείωται διὰ παθημάτων· ἐλέου γε μὴν τοῦ πάντας σώζειν ἐθέλοντος, ἐν τοῖς μετὰ τοῦτο καιροῖς, ὡς ἐν μηνὶ δευτέρῳ μεθέξουσι καὶ αὐτοὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ συνεορτάσουσι τοῖς ἁγίοις, τοῖς ἐν καιρῷ κεκλημένοις, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν· ἄθρει γὰρ ὅπως οἱ μὲν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ τὸν τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας εὐθὺς ἀποτριψάμενοι ῥύπον, σφάζουσι τὸν ἀμνὸν ἐν πρώτῳ μηνὶ, καὶ εἰς τὰς τοῦ πιστεύειν ἀρχὰς ἀναθρώσκουσιν. Οἱ δὲ κεχρισμένοι τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Κυρίου, παρ' οὐδὲν ἡγήσονται τὸν ὀλοθρευτὴν, καὶ ἀμείνους ἔσονται τῆς φθορᾶς. Οἱ δὲ, ὡς ἐν ἔτει τε καὶ ἐν μηνὶ δευτέρῳ, προσίασι μόλις καὶ ὁμολογοῦσι τὸν μολυσμόν. Καὶ ὅτι γεγόνασιν ἀκάθαρτοι ἐπὶ ψυχῇ ἀνθρώπου, διεβεβαιοῦντο σαφῶς, καὶ τῆς εὐλογίας ἀξιοῦσι τυχεῖν, ὕστερον δὲ καὶ μετὰ τοὺς πρώτους, πληροῦσι τὴν ἑορτήν· «Ὅταν γὰρ τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰσέλθῃ, φησὶ, τότε πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται.» Προαναπεφώνηκε δέ που καὶ ὁ προφήτης περὶ αὐτῶν· «Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐπιστρέψουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐπιζητήσουσι Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν αὐτῶν, καὶ Δαβὶδ τὸν βασιλέα αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκστήσονται ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς αὐτοῦ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν.» Ἐπιζητηθήσεται γὰρ ἐν ἐσχάτοις καιροῖς παρὰ τῶν ὑπολελειμμένων ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, ὁ ἐκ σπέρματος Δαβὶδ, κατὰ σάρκα Χριστός.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθὴς ὁ λόγος· τέθειται γὰρ ἐν ἐλπίσιν ὁ Ἰσραήλ.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ὅτι δὲ οὐκ ἀπλημμελὲς, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ τῶν ἄγαν σφαλερωτάτων, τὸ μὴ πληροῦν ἑορτὰς ἐπὶ Χριστῷ, διεσάφησεν εὐθὺ, τὸν μήτε ἀκάθαρτον ἐπὶ ψυχῇ ἀνθρώπου, μήτε μὴν ἐν ὁδῷ μακρᾷ γεγονότα, καὶ ἀναγκαῖον οὐκ ἔχοντα παραπόδισμα, ποιναῖς ταῖς ἐσχάταις ὑπενεχθήσεσθαι λέγων, εἰ μὴ δρᾷν ἕλοιτο τὰ νενομισμένα. Νοηθείη δ' ἂν πρὸς ἡμῶν ἀκάθαρτος μὲν ὡς ἐπ' ἀνθρώπου ψυχῇ, καθάπερ ἐλέγομεν ἀρτίως, ὁ κυριοκτόνος Ἰουδαῖος. Ἐν ὁδῷ δὲ ὥσπερ μακρᾷ, καὶ ἔξω που τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἤτοι τῆς ἁγίας τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἐκκλησίας, «Ὁ τῷ ξύλῳ λέγων, Θεός μου εἶ σὺ, καὶ τῷ λίθῳ λέγων, Σὺ ἐγέννησάς με.» Καὶ μέντοι τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα προσκυνῶν, ἤγουν ὁ ἑτέραν τινὰ νοσήσας πλάνησιν· εἴπερ ἐστὶν ἀληθὲς, ὡς ἀγχοῦ μὲν ὑπάρχων νοοῖτο Θεοῦ πᾶς ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς, καὶ ἀκιβδήλευτον ἔχων ἐπ' αὐτῷ τὴν δόξαν· ἐξέστηκε δὲ καὶ ἀποφοιτᾷ καὶ ἔστι μακρὰν πᾶς εἴ τις οὐχ ὧδε ἔχει. Οὐκοῦν οἱ μήτε ἀκάθαρτοι ἐπὶ ψυχῆς ἀνθρώπου κατὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους, μήτε μὴν ὄντες ἐν ὁδῷ μακρᾷ, καθ' Ἕλληνας ἢ αἱρετικοὺς, σπουδαίως τε καὶ ἀμελλητὶ προσοίσομεν τὴν θυσίαν, καὶ τὰς ἑορτὰς Κυρίου τι
pass_a_gloss: (in the month) the second completing the feast and slaying the victim, for a type of Christ, according to the law of the Passover, we will consider to be none other than the Jews, defiled by the blood-guilt against Christ, and having as indictment for uncleanness the having-outraged-in-drunkenness against Emmanuel. For such people slipped away necessarily from our holy feast. And they come late and have missed the season according to which the leader of the life of all was perfected through sufferings; but by the mercy of the one wishing to save all, in the seasons after this, as in a second month, they too will partake of Christ and will feast together with the saints, those called in season, and it is plain, those from the nations. For look how those in Egypt, having at once wiped off the filth of idolatry, slay the lamb in the first month and leap up to the beginnings of believing. And those anointed with the blood of the Lord will consider the destroyer as nothing and will be better than corruption. But the others, as in a year and month second, approach scarcely and confess the defilement. And that they have become unclean on a soul of a man they affirmed clearly, and they deem worthy to obtain the blessing, and later and after the first they fulfill the feast. For whenever the fullness of the nations enters, he says, then all Israel will be saved. And somewhere the prophet also proclaimed beforehand about them: And after these the sons of Israel will return and will seek the Lord their God and David their king, and they will be astonished at the Lord and at his goods at the last of the days. For in last seasons will be sought by those left over from Israel the one from the seed of David, Christ according to flesh. PALLADIUS: True the word; for Israel has been placed in hopes. CYRIL: And that it is not faultless, but rather among the very most perilous, not to fulfill feasts for Christ, he made clear at once, saying that the one neither unclean on a soul of a man, nor indeed having been in a long road, and not having a necessary hindrance, will be brought under the last penalties if he should not choose to do the things prescribed. And would be understood by us as unclean as on a soul of a man, just as we said just now, the Lord-killing Jew. And as in a long road and somewhere outside Jerusalem, or of the holy Church of our Savior, the one saying to the wood: You are my God, and saying to the stone: You begot me. And moreover the one worshiping the creation beside the creator, or the one who has been sick with some other wandering; if indeed it is true that every good man would be understood as being near God, and having the undebased glory (opinion) toward him; and has stood out and withdraws and is far, every one, if anyone does not hold thus. Therefore we, neither unclean on a soul of a man according to the Jews, nor indeed being in a long road according to Greeks or heretics, will zealously and without delay bring the sacrifice and will hon(or) the feasts of the Lord.
pass_b_english: Cyril: … second month, slaughtering the victim as a type of Christ according to the law of the Passover, we shall take to be none other than the Jews, defiled by the murder of Christ and having as the charge that makes them unclean their drunken outrage against Emmanuel. Such people, of necessity, slipped away from our holy feast. They come late, and have missed the season at which the author of the life of all was made perfect through sufferings (Hebrews 2:10). Yet by the mercy of the one who wills to save all (1 Timothy 2:4), in the times after this, as in a second month, they too will share in Christ and will keep the feast with the saints called at the proper time, that is, clearly, with those from the nations. For see how the people in Egypt at once rubbed off the filth of idolatry, slaughtered the lamb in the first month, and sprang up to the beginnings of faith. Those anointed with the blood of the Lord will count the destroyer as nothing and will prove stronger than corruption. But the others, as in the second year and in the second month, barely come at last and confess their defilement. They affirmed plainly that they had become unclean through a human soul, and they ask to be given the blessing; and later, after the first, they fulfill the feast. ‘For when the fullness of the nations has come in,’ it says, ‘then all Israel will be saved’ (Romans 11:25–26). And the prophet foretold about them somewhere: ‘And after these things the sons of Israel will return and will seek the Lord their God and David their king, and they will be amazed at the Lord and at his good things in the last days’ (Hosea 3:5). For in the last times Christ, of the seed of David according to the flesh, will be sought by those who are left of Israel.
Palladius: The word is true; for Israel has been set in hope.

Cyril: That it is not without fault, or rather that it is among the most perilous things of all, not to keep the feasts in Christ’s honor, he made clear at once, when he said that the one who is neither unclean through a human soul nor on a long journey, and has no necessary hindrance, will be brought under the utmost penalties if he does not choose to do what is prescribed. By the one unclean as through a human soul we may understand, as we were saying just now, the Jew who killed the Lord. And as on a long journey and somewhere outside Jerusalem, that is, the holy Church of our Savior, is ‘the one who says to the wood, You are my God, and to the stone, You have begotten me’ (Jeremiah 2:27); and also the one who worships the creation rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25), or anyone sick with some other error. For it is true that every good man is understood to be near God, holding a pure and undebased belief about him, while everyone who is not so has stood aside, withdrawn, and is far off. So we who are neither unclean through a human soul, like the Jews, nor on a long journey, like the pagans or the heretics, will earnestly and without delay offer the sacrifice and honor the feasts of the Lord.

choices.term: γραφὴν ἔχοντας εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν, τὸ ἐμπαροινῆσαι εἰς τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ
choices.english: having as the charge that makes them unclean their drunken outrage against Emmanuel
choices.why: γραφή here is a legal indictment.

choices.term: ἀκιβδήλευτον ἔχων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ τὴν δόξαν
choices.english: holding a pure and undebased belief about him
choices.why: δόξα here is opinion or belief, as the contrast with ‘other error’ shows.
Ἕλληνες in Cyril means non-Christian Gentiles.
The verb is split at the column break; it is rendered once, here at the end of §12.
